r90_proposal.lowest_axis_basis: Depth is the axis whose declared obligation was least met, and it is the axis the round's own synthesizer rules harmed. JAXIS's per-axis table recommends depth 'harmed (bounded)' at 1b09f3f on the same evidence this ledger indexes (D-D1 blocking: the doc corpus/fixtures/README.md names as the current contract is falsified by the delivered checker on exactly what C1 changed; C-D3: three r89-delivered r89-f2-* READMEs state pre-FN-1 expectations), and its admission recommendation is 'do not admit as-is; repair, then admit' with R1-R4, after which depth becomes improved (bounded) — the r88 sequence verbatim. Two independent reasons point the same way. First, C3's declared purpose was to govern JDEP3's three uncovered inspired-content classes, and the only seat that tested whether the delivered rows decide their own cases found all three undecided or partial (JDEP2: R8 uncovered, R9 uncovered, R10 partial; the probes replay CLEAN, so the gap is in the governing text, not the fixtures). Second, the harm is a recurrence: the boundary doc and the fixture index were repaired at 51b286b (Q88-024..027) and are stale again at 1b09f3f because the r89 wording change moved the checker without moving the instruction surface (E1's 15 drift items, CB1's R1-R15, JCAL5's doc_parity_check, H2 F5, H5). Calibration and coverage each met their declared claims (fixtures + combined summary + FN-1/2 for C1; 14/14 delivered anchors + ETCSL marker for C2) and their residue is smaller and local: calibration's is two one-line qualification defects plus one unfixtured branch (Q89-001/002/003), coverage's is one missing in-corpus map plus receipt and mode-label repairs (Q89-011/012/013). No seat rules any axis harmed other than depth, and none rules an axis unchanged, so this ordering rests on the harmed depth axis plus unmet obligations, not on a scalar.
